protocol.instrument_name: Protocol for Initiation of the Oral Contraceptive Pill
protocol.legal_basis: Drugs, Poisons and Controlled Substances Act 1981 and the Drugs, Poisons and Controlled Substances Regulations 2017 (the Regulations); supply of the Schedule 4 poisons documented in this Protocol for the initiation of the oral contraceptive pill under a structured prescribing arrangement; requirement of the Secretary Approval: Community Pharmacist Program that pharmacists comply with this Protocol and have completed the current training requirements specified in the departmental guidance before supplying Schedule 4 poisons (page 4, '1. About').
protocol.supervision_model: structured prescribing arrangement (document's own term) under the Secretary Approval: Community Pharmacist Program; pharmacists must operate at all times in accordance with the Drugs, Poisons and Controlled Substances Act 1981, the Regulations and all other applicable Victorian, Commonwealth and national laws, and act in a manner consistent with the Pharmacy Board of Australia's Code of Conduct (page 4, '1. About').
protocol.scope_summary: Victorian Community Pharmacist Program protocol (July 2026) authorising pharmacists to supply Schedule 4 poisons for commencement or restarting of an oral contraceptive pill only. Scope of the service is limited to pharmacist-led commencement or restarting of an oral contraceptive pill; it does not cover resupply of other contraceptive methods (page 5, '2.1. Key to colours used in this protocol'). Includes a flowchart (pages 5-9), supplementary assessment guidance (sections 4-5, pages 12-21), a Medicines List (page 22-23), counselling/documentation requirements (pages 10, 24-25) and follow-up rules (page 26).

steps.description: 'Confirm informed consent and undertake contraceptive counselling; The pharmacist must provide patient centred contraceptive counselling and support shared decision-making, including but not limited to: All available contraceptive options, including options not available through this service e.g. LARCs, combined hormonal vaginal ring and DMPA injection; Relative effectiveness, adherence requirements and additional benefits e.g. desire for bleeding control and duration of need; Confirmation that contraceptive and sexual health plan may include OCP; Relevant costs e.g. medicines; Communication with the patient's usual GP. Where the patient does not have a regular GP, support them to identify a local general practice using the Healthdirect Service Finder.' No branch -> 'Refer to General Practitioner'.

gates.criterion: Informed consent confirmed and patient-centred contraceptive counselling / shared decision-making completed

steps.description: 'Patient history; take a focused history to identify relevant risk factors:' Age; Medical history (VTE, migraine, cardiovascular disease, liver disease, cancer, meningioma); Family history (VTE in first-degree relative <45-50 years); Social history, including mental health and any identified safety concerns; Smoking status; Menopausal or perimenopausal status, especially for women in their 40's; Medication history, including current and recently ceased medicines, use of enzyme-inducing medicines, and previous hormonal contraceptives, including the indication for use, tolerability, adverse effects (including mood-related symptoms), and reason for cessation or change; Reproductive history (LMP, pregnancy risk, postpartum/lactation status); Medication allergies and/or adverse reactions; Review MHR, where possible; STI assessment and referral (recommended for anyone who is sexually active and engaging in unprotected sex, has a new partner since their last STI test, or thinks they may be at risk).

gates.criterion: Patient able to provide a history ('If the patient is unable to provide a history, refer to GP')

provenance.section_heading: 2.1. Key to colours used in this protocol

steps.description: 'Conduct Clinical Review and Record findings' - Measure BP; Calculate BMI; 'Exclude pregnancy with high confidence. Consider if emergency contraception is required.' (see PW-2 for the printed pregnancy-exclusion criteria, page 15); 'Taking into account the patient's history, clinical review, and clinical judgement, the pharmacist should identify UKMEC risk factors and assign an eligibility category. The highest UKMEC category determines a contraceptive option's suitability'. Supplementary note (page 16, '4.3. Examination'): 'A single elevated BP reading is not enough to classify a patient as hypertensive, and a second BP reading should be taken at the end of the consultation.'

steps.description: 'Does the patient meet any of the following exclusion criteria?' (list reproduced in eligibility.exclusion EXC-1 to EXC-13): UKMEC category 3 or 4; changes in health that would be a contraindication to ongoing use; potential pregnancy; drug interactions that may compromise efficacy; prior significant side effects related to hormonal contraceptive use; SBP>140mmHg or DBP>90mmHg; BMI of more than 35kg/m2; current or history of meningioma; signs and symptoms of PMOS/PCOS; endometriosis; unexplained vaginal bleeding/menstrual bleeding/pain/irregular periods/amenorrhea/pain with intercourse; symptoms of STI; requests or requires a method of contraception not available in the Oral Contraceptive Service. Yes -> 'Refer to General Practitioner'. No, to all -> continue to PW-1-S9.

gates.criterion: Patient meets NO exclusion criteria (all of EXC-1 to EXC-13 absent)

steps.description: 'Pharmacotherapy' - 'If the contraceptive plan aligns, select an oral contraceptive option in accordance with the Therapeutic Guidelines: Sexual and Reproductive Health (Contraception) and the Australian Medicines Handbook: Combined Oral Contraceptives. Pharmacists may only supply OCPs listed in this protocol.' 'For most eligible patients without additional risk factors, a monophasic COCP containing 30 micrograms of ethinylestradiol with levonorgestrel is recommended as first-line therapy.' Flowchart medicines list (page 8): Combined Oral Contraceptive Pills - Low dose estrogen: ethinylestradiol + levonorgestrel 20/100microg; ethinylestradiol + drospirenone 20microg/3mg; estradiol + nomegestrol 1.5/2.5mg. Standard dose estrogen: ethinylestradiol + levonorgestrel 30/150microg; ethinylestradiol + desogestrel 30/150microg; ethinylestradiol + dienogest 30microg/2mg; ethinylestradiol + drospirenone 30microg/3mg; ethinylestradiol + gestodene 30/75microg; ethinylestradiol + cyproterone 35microg/2mg; ethinylestradiol + norethisterone 35microg/0.5mg; ethinylestradiol + norethisterone 35microg/1mg; estetrol + drospirenone 14.2/3mg. Triphasic: ethinylestradiol 30/40/30microg + levonorgestrel 50/75/125microg. Quadriphasic: estradiol valerate 3/2/2/1mg + dienogest 2/3mg. Progesterone Only Pills (POPs): levonorgestrel 30microg; norethisterone 350microg; drospirenone 4mg. Age gate for a COCP (page 19, 'C. Age-related eligibility for a COCP'): 'Patients aged 18 to 40 years: A COCP may be initiated where the patient meets all protocol and UKMEC eligibility requirements.'

gates.criterion: The contraceptive plan aligns with the Therapeutic Guidelines: Sexual and Reproductive Health (Contraception) and Australian Medicines Handbook: Combined Oral Contraceptives; and (for a COCP) the patient is aged 18 to 40 years and meets all protocol and UKMEC eligibility requirements

diagnosis_pathways.name: Assess pregnancy risk - pregnancy exclusion before commencing any hormonal contraception

steps.description: 'Assess pregnancy risk - Pregnancy should be reasonably excluded before commencing any hormonal contraception. A patient can be reasonably assumed not to be pregnant if: There are no symptoms or signs of pregnancy AND any of the following criteria are met: they have not had intercourse since the start of the last normal (natural) menstrual period, or since childbirth, abortion or miscarriage; they have been correctly and consistently using a reliable method of contraception (barrier methods can be assumed to be reliable if used correctly in this context); they are within the first 5 days of the onset of a normal (natural) menstrual period or within the first 5 days after abortion or miscarriage; they are less than 21 days postpartum; they have not had intercourse for >21 days and have a negative urine pregnancy test. 'If there is any doubt regarding whether the patient may be pregnant, hormonal contraception should NOT be supplied and the patient referred to an appropriate healthcare provider for pregnancy testing.'

gates.criterion: No symptoms or signs of pregnancy AND any one of the five printed criteria met (no intercourse since start of last normal menstrual period or since childbirth/abortion/miscarriage; correctly and consistently using a reliable method of contraception; within the first 5 days of onset of a normal menstrual period or within the first 5 days after abortion or miscarriage; less than 21 days postpartum; not had intercourse for >21 days and a negative urine pregnancy test)

open_questions.observed: Flowchart prints 'Is the patient, female*, aged >= 18-50 years of age?' with '>= ' combined with an upper bound of 50; section C separately states 'Patients aged 18 to 40 years: A COCP may be initiated' and 'Patients aged 41 to 50 years: Pharmacists must not initiate a combined hormonal contraception in this age group'.
open_questions.why_unclear: The '>= 18-50' phrasing is not standard; it is read as an inclusive 18-50 service range. Age bounds recorded as min 18 / max 50. The COCP-specific 18-40 sub-range is captured as a pathway gate (PW-1-S11) and as EXC-15/RF-27 rather than as the service age bound.

open_questions.observed: Page 7: Yes branch of the 'treat and refer' box reads 'Proceed & refer to GP for immediate review', while the No branch reads 'No: Continue to pg. 8'.
open_questions.why_unclear: It is not explicit whether the pharmacist proceeds to pharmacotherapy in the same consultation when a 'treat and refer' criterion is met, or whether supply is deferred until GP review. Both readings recorded; EXE-1/EXE-2 confidence set to unclear.

open_questions.topic: Medicines List table row alignment (grouped cells)
open_questions.observed: In the text extraction of the page 22 table, the estrogen column cell is blank for the drospirenone 3000 row (low-dose group) and for the desogestrel/dienogest/drospirenone/gestodene rows (standard-dose group); doses appear as bare numbers under column headers 'Estrogen dose (micrograms)' and 'Progestogen dose (micrograms)'; the estetrol row prints '14200 (14.2 mg)'.
open_questions.why_unclear: Blank cells read as grouped/merged cells inheriting the row above ('ethinylestradiol 20' and 'ethinylestradiol 30' respectively); corroborated by the page 8 list which prints the same pairings with explicit units. Rows affected are recorded with confidence 'medium'.

open_questions.topic: No dose, frequency or duration printed in the Medicines List
open_questions.observed: The page 22 table prints only estrogen/progestogen doses and brand name examples; no per-dose amount, frequency, duration or pack quantity is printed for any row.
open_questions.why_unclear: Dose/frequency/duration/max_quantity/max_dose left empty rather than inferred. Quantity to supply taken from page 9 ('Provide one original pack (a 3-4 month supply)'). Dosing is deferred by the protocol to Therapeutic Guidelines: Sexual and Reproductive Health (Contraception) and Australian Medicines Handbook (page 17).

open_questions.topic: Action not specified for 'when to seek further care' triggers
open_questions.observed: Page 24 lists under 'When to seek further care and/or treatment': 'Signs of VTE and what to do if it is suspected' and 'The importance of reporting new or worsening mood-related symptoms', without stating a referral destination or urgency.
open_questions.why_unclear: RF-32 and RF-33 actions (REFER / REVIEW_GP) are the closest enum values; the document specifies neither destination nor urgency, so confidence is 'unclear' and severity kept at 'medium' (not upgraded).

open_questions.topic: No emergency referral pathway in this document
open_questions.observed: The protocol's referral options are GP, other authorised prescribing health practitioners, women's health services, sexual health clinic, hospital, support services and pregnancy testing providers; no emergency/ambulance/000 escalation is printed anywhere in the 28 pages.
open_questions.why_unclear: referral.emergency is empty because the document genuinely contains none (not a transcription gap).

open_questions.topic: Eligibility of people not presumed female at birth
open_questions.observed: Flowchart gate is 'female* ... all people presumed female at birth'; page 14 separately addresses 'Contraceptive options for transgender and non-binary people' and states information on cervical screening should be provided to transgender men and non-binary people who have a uterus.
open_questions.why_unclear: The document does not explicitly state how the 'female (presumed female at birth)' gate applies to transgender men / non-binary people with a uterus seeking oral contraception; the supplementary note says such patients 'may require referral' where they receive gender-affirming hormone therapy or have more complex hormonal management needs.

open_questions.topic: Quadriphasic strength printed in different units on page 8 vs page 22
open_questions.observed: Page 8 prints 'Estradiol Valerate 3/2/2/1mg + Dienogest 2/3mg'; the page 22 Medicines List table prints the same Qlaira row as estradiol valerate '3000/2000/2000/1000' and dienogest '2000/3000' under column headers '(micrograms)'.
open_questions.why_unclear: Same product, two printed unit presentations (mg vs micrograms). No conversion applied; the page 22 microgram figures are transcribed for TX-14 and the page 8 mg wording is quoted in the pathway step. Confirm which presentation the rules engine should display.

open_questions.observed: referral.routine and referral.urgent quote destinations printed across pages 5, 13, 14, 15, 20, 21, 24, 25 and 26; the shared provenance object references the first page (5).
open_questions.why_unclear: Single shared provenance per schema; page range recorded here as required by the spec.

open_questions.topic: Personal/family history of breast cancer screening advice
open_questions.observed: Page 25: 'People who have a personal or family history of breast cancer should be advised to see their medical practitioner for advice regarding frequency and type of screening.'
open_questions.why_unclear: This is screening advice rather than a service exclusion or escalation trigger; it is captured in referral.routine only, not as a red flag.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Authorisation status under the Secretary Approval: Community Pharmacist Program and the 'structured prescribing arrangement' supervision model.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Supervision model is the document's own term; confirm local authorisation/credentialing before go-live.

hugh_to_confirm.item: 'Where the protocol indicates to Refer to General Practitioner, the Pharmacist may refer to other authorised prescribing health practitioners where they have the appropriate women's health, sexual health or contraceptive expertise.'
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Who qualifies as having 'appropriate expertise' is left to pharmacist judgement/local policy.

hugh_to_confirm.item: 'Where timely access is not available, referral to other women's health services may be considered, including women's sexual and reproductive health hubs, women's health clinics, the Aboriginal women's health clinic, or the virtual women's health clinic.'
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Hedged ('may be considered') and dependent on local service availability.

hugh_to_confirm.item: 'Review MHR, where possible' and 'ensure MHR upload (if applicable)'.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Conditional on My Health Record access/consent and pharmacy software configuration; confirm local workflow.

hugh_to_confirm.item: 'If required, emergency contraception may be supplied as per standard pharmacy care, or the person may be referred ... for another method of emergency contraception e.g. insertion of a copper intrauterine device.'
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Emergency contraception is outside this protocol's Medicines List; local policy must define what 'standard pharmacy care' means here.

hugh_to_confirm.item: 'The UKMEC calculator should be used to ensure all possible contraindications are considered prior to hormonal contraception selection.'
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Depends on an external calculator and the currency of UKMEC; confirm which version/tool is approved for use.

hugh_to_confirm.item: 'Provide one original pack (a 3-4 month supply)' and 'Dispense medications via pharmacy dispensing program and ensure MHR upload (if applicable)'.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Supply quantity and dispensing-program mechanics are operational rules to confirm against current program instructions and software.

hugh_to_confirm.item: STI assessment and referral: 'recommended for anyone who is sexually active and engaging in unprotected sex, has a new partner since their last STI test, or thinks they may be at risk' and 'Approved pharmacists should recommend STI testing for individuals who may be at risk even if the individual does not report any symptoms.'
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Worded as 'recommended'; thresholds for testing/referral are left to pharmacist judgement.

hugh_to_confirm.item: 'Pharmacists are also expected to exercise professional judgment in adapting treatment guidelines to presenting circumstances.'
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Explicit local-judgement latitude; confirm what adaptation is permitted before go-live.
